title: rustfs-gateway conformance case
description: Frozen schema (schema_version 1) for a single rustfs-gateway conformance case. Cases are authored as TOML; this JSON Schema validates the parsed TOML document, so the same contract governs the TOML files on disk and any JSON tooling built on top of them. See conformance/README.md for the freeze policy and the change procedure.

exchanges.description: Multi-request form. Use together with connection.reuse to pin keep-alive behaviour, or to capture a value (upload id, continuation token) from one response and interpolate it into the next request.

id.description: c-<domain>-<NNNN>. The domain segment must equal the directory the file lives in, and the file must be named <id>.toml.

schema_version.description: Frozen at 1. A runner MUST reject a case whose schema_version it does not know, with an explicit 'update the runner' error - never by ignoring unknown fields.

rationale.description: MANDATORY. Why this case exists, in a form that lets a future maintainer decide whether it may be deleted. A case without a rationale is unmaintainable and the runner must refuse to load it.

evidence.description: MANDATORY. Where the asserted behaviour was observed. Compliance: URL plus an original one-line summary only. Never paste upstream issue or PR prose.

quirks.description: Quirk ids from model/overlays/*.toml that this case exercises. The mutation gate builds its quirk -> case coverage matrix from this field; a quirk no case references fails CI. May be empty only while model/overlays/ does not yet contain the corresponding entry.

polarity.description: positive = asserts required behaviour on a well-formed input. negative = asserts refusal, error shape, or safe termination on a hostile or malformed input. The suite requires negative >= positive.

operation.description: AWS operation name, for coverage matrices. Omit for cases below the operation layer (framing, signing, routing).

tags.description: Free-form by design: the vocabulary lives in conformance/README.md and a lint, not in this schema, so adding a tag is not a schema change. 'slow' is reserved and moves a case out of the PR gate.

applies_to.description: Applicability gates. The rustfs-gateway assembly path (--transport hyper|conn) is deliberately NOT expressible here: every case runs on every assembly path and the two runs must agree.

http_versions.description: Defaults to both. Narrow it when the case is about framing that only one version has.

tls.description: required: only meaningful over TLS (SSE-C header gating, session resumption). forbidden: only meaningful in cleartext (plaintext downgrade, h2c prior knowledge). Default any.

profiles.description: Defaults to all. Use when implementations legitimately diverge and the divergence is documented in the rationale.

timeout_ms.description: Whole-case wall-clock budget. Exceeding it is a case failure of kind 'hang', not an environment error.

url.description: Stable link to the source of the behavioural fact.

summary.description: One original sentence, written by the case author. The 200-character ceiling is a compliance control, not a style preference: it makes pasting upstream prose structurally impossible.

setup.description: Preconditions established before the case runs. Setup traffic is NOT under test: the runner may use normalised, correctly signed requests for it. Anything the case actually asserts must be in request/exchanges.

absent.description: Assert the bucket does not exist; delete it if it does.
Assert the key does not exist. Required for If-None-Match style cases whose meaning depends on absence.

capture_upload_id_as.description: Bind the created upload id to a capture name so requests can interpolate ${capture.<name>}.

fault.description: A failure the backend is to produce at a named point inside one operation. Every other setup declaration describes state that was already true when the request arrived, and a fault that was already true is refused with its own status before any of the response has gone out. This is the only way the corpus can describe a failure discovered after that point.

operation.description: The operation that fails. Named here rather than read from case.operation because a case with several exchanges must be able to say which one of them fails.

at.description: after_commit: the operation passes every check that can still choose a status, its response head goes out carrying the success status, and only then does the work fail. The failure reaches the client as a document inside a success, which is what expect.kind = 'stream_error' with stream_termination = 'error_document' observes. no_progress_after_commit: the same head goes out and the work then never finishes at all, so there is no failure for the backend to report and the response can only be ended by a bound outside it. Both points exist only for an operation AWS documents as flushing its head early; for any other neither exists, and a case naming one is refused rather than quietly run as an ordinary refusal.

code.description: The S3 error code the work reports. It travels in the body under the committed status, never as the status: by the time this code exists the status line has been sent. Required for at = 'after_commit' and forbidden for at = 'no_progress_after_commit', where the backend reports nothing at all and any code named here would be a code no implementation could produce.

clock.description: Clock injection. Needed for clock-skew and presigned-expiry cases - and also for every byte-exact body assertion whose response embeds a timestamp (LastModified, Expires).

fixed.description: RFC3339 UTC, quoted. MUST be a quoted TOML string, not a bare TOML datetime, so that the on-disk case and its JSON projection are the same value. This is the wall clock the system under test observes.

skew_ms.description: Offset applied to the clock the system under test observes, relative to the runner. May be negative.

request_time.description: The instant the client claims: what goes into x-amz-date and the credential scope. Distinct from 'fixed' on purpose - a skew case pins both ends independently.

reuse.description: true: every exchange runs on one connection and the runner fails the case if the connection is torn down between exchanges. false: a fresh connection per exchange.

pipeline.description: Write the next request before reading the previous response.

read_window_bytes.description: Backpressure knob: the runner stops reading once this many unread response bytes are buffered, so a server that ignores flow control is observable.

close_notify.description: false tears the TCP connection down without a TLS close_notify - the truncation attack shape. A correct server must not treat a truncated stream as a complete body.

requestSpec.description: One request. Either a structured form (method + target + headers) or a raw head. Every string field may contain ${capture.<name>} references; interpolation happens BEFORE signing, so an interpolated value is covered by the signature.

target.description: Raw request-target, sent verbatim. Deliberately not a parsed URL: encoding form is frequently the thing under test.

host.description: Overrides Host / :authority, including malformed or absent values.

raw_headers.description: Ordered, duplicate-preserving header list as [name, value] pairs. Use when order or duplication is the subject of the case.

raw_head_utf8.description: Entire request head verbatim, including the request line and CRLFs. Escape hatch for malformed framing and request smuggling vectors.

chunks.description: Body delivered as a timed sequence. Mutually exclusive with 'body'. Truncation is expressed compositionally - declare a length in headers, send fewer bytes, then a control chunk - rather than as its own action.

h2_frames.description: Frame-level scripting. Only valid when case.applies_to.http_versions is exactly ["h2"].

signSpec.description: How the runner signs. Signing is computed by the runner, not hand-written into the case, so that a case stays readable and does not rot when a fixture changes. Negative signature cases sign correctly and then tamper with exactly one canonical component.

mode.description: 'anonymous' sends no credential at all. 'none' means the case supplies its own Authorization bytes verbatim and the runner must not touch them.

signed_headers.description: Explicit SignedHeaders list. Use to under-sign deliberately (the complement-of-a-denylist bypass shape).

tamper.description: Applied AFTER a correct signature is computed. Exactly one canonical component changes, so a failure names the component rather than 'the signature was wrong somewhere'.

target.description: Which query parameter or header name the component refers to.

dataChunk.description: One unit of body data. 'utf8'/'hex'/'file' carry the LOGICAL payload: when sign.mode is a streaming mode the runner adds aws-chunked framing and per-chunk signatures. 'raw_utf8'/'raw_hex' bypass framing entirely and go on the wire byte for byte.

delay_ms.description: Wall-clock pause before this chunk is written. This is the field that makes arrival timing - and therefore chunk state machines, backpressure and timeouts - expressible at all.

action.description: close: full close, the outcome becomes unobservable to the client - use only when 'no 200 was received' is the whole assertion. half_close: shutdown(WR), the server can still answer, which is what makes an abrupt-termination case assertable. rst: TCP reset. stall: hold the connection open and send nothing. stop_reading/resume_reading: induce and release backpressure.

payload.description: A byte string. Exactly one source.

fill.description: Byte pattern repeated to reach 'size'. Defaults to a deterministic pattern.

relPath.description: Path relative to conformance/. No parent traversal.

headerMap.description: Header name -> value. A value may be a list to express a repeated header. In expectations the value "*" asserts presence with any value.

repeat.description: Run this identical request and expectation this many times. Used for cache and retry contracts where one exchange proves nothing.

kind.description: response: a complete response, success or error, head and body intact. stream_error: the operation failed AFTER the response head was committed - either an error document inside a success status, or an abrupt end of the body. event_stream: a framed event sequence. hang: no complete response within case.timeout_ms; only ever asserted to document a known defect of a foreign implementation, never as required behaviour. connection_reset: the peer reset without a response.

stream_termination.description: How a stream_error ended. Distinguishes 'a 200 that carries an <Error>' from 'the body just stopped', which are different bugs with the same symptom.

code.description: S3 error code, e.g. SignatureDoesNotMatch. Asserted against the <Code> element, not the status alone.

headers_exact.description: The complete header set. Any header not listed is a failure. Hop-by-hop headers the runner itself adds are excluded; conformance/README.md lists them.

header_order.description: Relative order of the listed headers on the wire.

header_name_bytes_exact.description: Compare header names case-sensitively, byte for byte, instead of case-insensitively.

body_bytes_before_error.description: RESPONSE body bytes received before the stream_error marker. Required when kind is stream_error. Not to be confused with request_progress.body_bytes_sent_at_response, which is the client-side counterpart.

timing.description: Time-domain assertions. terminate_within_ms is the assertion that catches the client-hang family, which no status-code assertion can see.

request_progress.description: What the client had managed to send when the response head arrived. This is how 'the server rejected before consuming the body' becomes assertable.

connection_after.description: State of the connection once the exchange finished. 'open' asserts the connection stayed reusable.

capture.description: Bind values out of this response for later exchanges to interpolate as ${capture.<name>}. Necessary for anything with a server-minted opaque value: upload ids, continuation tokens, version ids.

xml_text.description: Text of the first element with this name.

bodyExpectation.description: Body assertions. Byte-exactness is the first-class citizen: exact_utf8 / exact_hex / golden compare the wire bytes. The 'xml' block is an additive diagnostic aid, never a substitute - a case that only asserts parsed structure cannot catch an element-order, xmlns, or empty-element regression.

redact.description: XML element names whose text is replaced by __REDACTED__ in both the observed body and the expectation before comparison. The element's presence and position are still asserted byte for byte. Without this, no response containing a server-minted opaque value could ever be pinned to bytes.
